newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX continues downtrend in limp trading.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX continues downtrend in limp trading.

text.p: Slovak blue chips were mostly quiet in flat trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Thursday, with the 16-share SAX index dipping 0.56 points to close at 189.93.
Some brokers said they saw signs of higher activity on the market, although overall trading figures remained low, boosted only by direct trades.
"Generally, the share prices are constantly falling, but I think they're close to a level which can attract the foreign investors," Dusan Sykora of ING Barings said.
He said foreign traders were currently mainly selling their shares, but added that some were looking to buy.
"So far, it has failed to change the overall picture, but I think it can be just a matter of time and we'll see improvement," Sykora added.
The session on the bourse floor was dominated by oil refinery Slovnaft, which traded 3,500 shares and closed down 15 crowns at 1,000, while other major issues mostly did not trade on Thursday.
Overall, volume increased to 503,260 shares, from 228,523 on Wednesday, while turnover jumped to 559.97 million crowns from 57.43 million.
